doc_name: Fencing at the 1908 Summer Olympics – Men's sabre
text: The men's sabre was one of four fencing events at the 1908 Summer Olympics programme and marked its fourth appearance, making it the only fencing event held at every Summer Olympics. The top two positions in the individual event were claimed by Hungarian fencers: Jenő Fuchs won gold and Béla Zulawszky took silver, while bronze was awarded to Bohemian Vilém Goppold von Lobsdorf. A total of 76 competitors from 11 nations participated, with each nation allowed to enter up to 12 fencers. This was the fourth time the event was held, and Georges de la Falaise of France, the 1900 gold medalist, returned after skipping the 1904 Games. Belgium, Bohemia, Great Britain, the Netherlands, and South Africa each made their debut in the men's sabre, while Austria made its third appearance, having missed only the 1904 Games. The competition consisted of four rounds, with each pool conducting a round-robin format to three touches. European sabre rules at the time used a full-body target area, unlike the above-the-waist target used in the 1904 Games, which later became standard post-World War I. Barrages were used to determine advancement when necessary. The first round featured pool sizes ranging from 4 to 8 fencers, with the three fencers who lost the fewest bouts advancing; a three-way tie for two spots led to the elimination of the British fencer. Renaud lost both playoff matches, allowing Grade and Jack to advance, while Lichtenfels suffered two losses in the playoff. The fifth pool had only four fencers, resulting in only one elimination—Langevin. Petri defeated van Tomme in the playoff for third place after losing to the Belgian in the main pool, and Badman defeated van Minden in the playoff for third place. The tenth pool, the largest at twice the size of the fifth, had eight fencers, with five eliminated; von Lobsdorf defeated all seven of his opponents to win first place, with no match between Sarzano and Stohr. Chapuis was eliminated in the three-way playoff for second and third. The final pool included seven fencers. Eight second-round pools were held, ranging from 4 to 5 fencers. Notley won two playoff matches to secure second place in his pool and advance. Doorman, who had lost to Petri in the main pool, defeated the German in the playoff for second place. Two semifinals, each with eight fencers, were held, with the top four from each advancing to the final. Four fencers tied at 5-2 records and all advanced to the final; Ceccherini withdrew after his first four bouts, resulting in walkover wins for Tóth, van der Voodt, and Doorman. Fuchs and von Lobsdorf did not finish within the time limit and were both recorded as losers. The gold medal playoff was won by Fuchs, who secured victory with a one-touch bout decided by a parry and riposte to his fellow Hungarian's head.
